verdict.rationale: Apify documents a convenience call that starts an Actor and waits for it to finish, webhooks that fire when a run finishes, and an Actor input (maxCrawlPages) plus a retrieval limit parameter that cap how much is gathered. Together these give coarse control over when results arrive and how complete they are, but there is no documented, explicit latency-versus-completeness control such as a configurable wait timeout or returning partial results early. Missing for 10: explicit wait/timeout parameters for returning partial results, documented guidance on the latency/completeness tradeoff, platform-level (not Actor-specific) crawl-size controls, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trade off latency against completeness by controlling exactly when content is returned

citations.quote: Starts an Actor and waits for it to finish.
Use the limit parameter to retrieve a specific number of results.
you can use webhooks to start another Actor when an Actor run finishes or fails.
